direct_answer: Aker BP integrates sustainability-related performance into its variable remuneration through the company-wide bonus programme, which is paid to all permanent employees, including management [Source 1]. The bonus scheme is based on a set of key performance indicators (KPIs) used in the performance management system; these include sustainability-related KPIs such as Safety (serious incidents per 1 million work hours) and Equity share scope 1 GHG intensity (kg CO2e/boe) [Source 1]. Aker BP states that approximately 22% of the bonus potential is dependent on sustainability-related initiatives and targets, and that the same share of bonus potential applies for all employees [Source 1]. Governance-wise, the Organisational Development and Compensation Committee (ODCC) is responsible for ensuring remuneration arrangements support the company’s strategy, including sustainability matters [Source 2], and it oversees the setting of targets and monitoring of progress related to KPIs linked to the incentive schemes for executive management team (EMT) remuneration [Source 3].
compliance_rationale: The passages provide evidence that sustainability-related KPIs are part of the bonus scheme and quantify the share of bonus potential linked to sustainability-related initiatives/targets (22%) [Source 1], and they describe ODCC oversight for EMT incentive-linked KPIs [Source 3] and ODCC’s role in aligning remuneration with strategy including sustainability [Source 2]. However, the retrieved passages do not specify the full set of GOV-3 details for administrative, management and supervisory bodies (e.g., whether/how the board’s own remuneration is linked to sustainability, detailed scheme characteristics for those bodies, and the approval/update level for the incentive terms).
disclosure_gaps: Whether members of the Board of Directors / supervisory bodies have sustainability-linked incentive/remuneration arrangements (the evidence only clearly covers employees/management and EMT-linked KPIs, not BoD remuneration).

Key characteristics of the incentive/remuneration schemes specifically for administrative, management and supervisory bodies (e.g., payout mechanics, time horizons, malus/clawback, weighting across metrics) beyond the general statement that a bonus programme exists.

Whether performance is assessed against specific sustainability-related targets/impacts for the administrative, management and supervisory bodies, and which exact targets/thresholds apply (beyond naming example KPIs such as safety and scope 1 GHG intensity).

Whether and how sustainability-related performance metrics are used as benchmarks or embedded in remuneration policies for the administrative, management and supervisory bodies (beyond ODCC oversight statements).

The proportion of variable remuneration dependent on sustainability-related targets/impacts for each relevant body/member category (22% is stated for the bonus potential generally, but not broken down by body or role).
The level in the undertaking at which the terms of incentive schemes are approved and updated (e.g., BoD vs general meeting), as required by GOV-3.
key_findings: Aker BP’s bonus programme (variable remuneration) applies to all permanent employees, including management, with the same share of bonus potential for all employees [Source 1].

Sustainability-related KPIs included in the KPI set used for the bonus scheme include Safety (serious incidents per 1 million work hours) and Equity share scope 1 GHG intensity (kg CO2e/boe) [Source 1].
Approximately 22% of the bonus potential is dependent on sustainability-related initiatives and targets [Source 1].
The ODCC is responsible for ensuring remuneration arrangements support the company’s strategy, including sustainability matters [Source 2].
The ODCC oversees target-setting and monitoring of progress for KPIs linked to incentive schemes for EMT remuneration [Source 3].
